Includes outcome and post-publication wording such as mortality, clinical worsening, 15 days, efficacy, effect, and failed reduce, despite the registered search needing P/I/C/design only.

Uses extensive NOT exclusions that can remove eligible RCT reports, secondary analyses linked to trial reports, or articles mentioning excluded terms such as antibodies, biomarkers, baricitinib, colchicine, comparison, review, or meta-analysis in the title.

Omits important synonyms and spelling variants: SARS-CoV-2, COVID19, COVID 19, 2019-nCoV, hospitalized/hospitalised, inpatient/in-patient, admitted/admission, Actemra, RoActemra, atlizumab, RG1569, and IL-6 receptor antagonist wording.

Uses inconsistent capitalization and overly narrow title terms such as Patients, Severe, Pneumonia, Usual Care, Adults, and Clinical Worsening, which are not necessary eligibility concepts and reduce sensitivity.
The third PubMed query includes remdesivir and other title fragments that may distort retrieval away from the tocilizumab-versus-usual-care/placebo question.
Current ClinicalTrials.gov terms are reasonable but narrow: the intervention field lacks brand names and IL-6 receptor antagonist synonyms, and the condition field lacks SARS-CoV-2/COVID19 variants.

It avoids outcome, date, language, comparator, blinding, oral-route, and named-trial restrictions.
concepts: Population/condition: postpartum haemorrhage/hemorrhage and spelling variants, including puerperal, obstetric, and maternal bleeding terms.
Intervention: tranexamic acid, abbreviations, chemical names, antifibrinolytic class terms, and common brand names.

weaknesses_of_current: The main PubMed query is too narrow because it requires WOMAN or the outcome phrase death due to bleeding; outcomes should not be part of the search strategy.
It omits MeSH terms such as "Postpartum Hemorrhage"[Mesh] and "Tranexamic Acid"[Mesh].
It uses only a few postpartum haemorrhage spelling variants and misses post partum, puerperal, obstetric/maternal bleeding, and truncation-based haemorrhage/hemorrhage variants.
It omits intervention synonyms including TXA, chemical-name variants, antifibrinolytic class terms, and brand names.

The randomized-trial component is weak and not equivalent to the Cochrane highly sensitive filter; it misses publication types, placebo, randomly, groups, drug therapy subheading, and animal-only exclusion.
The second PubMed query wrongly restricts to oral tranexamic acid and adjunct wording, which is not part of the review eligibility and can miss IV or unspecified-route trials.
The second PubMed query is an unstructured keyword string and lacks MeSH terms, spelling variants, brand names, class terms, and a validated RCT filter.
The third PubMed query targets a named trial/acronym, which should not be used in a comprehensive registered search and risks circular retrieval.

The ClinicalTrials.gov query is reasonable but could be made more sensitive by adding haemorrhage spelling variants, post-partum/post partum variants, puerperal/obstetric haemorrhage terms, TXA, brand names, and antifibrinolytic class terms.
